qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary big-ticket purchase deferrable in recessions; passenger airlines are explicitly classified as deferrable cyclicals under Gate 2.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Reject Standard: True discretionary big-ticket or deferrable cyclicals — airlines). Commercial passenger air travel is a highly cyclical, deferrable expenditure subject to severe demand volatility during economic downturns, high operating leverage, and intense price competition.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 7.8% is far below the 12% hurdle. Even during post-pandemic recovery (FY2024-2025 pre-tax margins of 7.3-8.1%), capital expenditures on aircraft fleet renewal absorb massive cash flow, while debt and finance leases (~$25B) remain heavy. Commercial passenger airlines are explicitly categorized under Gate 2 reject criteria as deferrable cyclicals lacking essential, non-discretionary demand insulation.
